telegram.token_hint: Kept as a secret in this profile's Hermes files and never shown again.

discord.intro: The agent answers through a Discord bot you make in the developer portal. The hub asks Discord about the bot before it stores the token.
discord.step1: Open the Discord developer portal, press New Application and pick a name.
discord.step2: Under Bot, press Reset Token and copy it. On the same page, turn on Message Content Intent.
discord.step3: Under OAuth2 → URL Generator pick the scopes bot and applications.commands, then Send Messages and Read Message History, and open the link to add the bot to your server.
discord.step4: Paste the token here, and your Discord user id (turn on Developer Mode, right-click your name → Copy User ID).

discord.how: Add the bot to your server with the link from the developer portal if you have not, then DM it or @mention it in a channel.

slack.intro: The agent answers through a Slack app you make. The hub asks Slack about both tokens before it stores them.
slack.step1: Open api.slack.com/apps, press Create New App → From scratch and pick your Slack team.
slack.step2: Under Socket Mode, turn it on and create an app-level token with connections:write (it starts with xapp-).
slack.step3: Under OAuth & Permissions add the bot scopes chat:write, app_mentions:read, channels:history, im:history, im:read, im:write and users:read.
slack.step4: Under Event Subscriptions, turn them on and subscribe to app_mention, message.im and message.channels; under App Home, turn on the Messages tab.
slack.step5: Press the Install button on the OAuth & Permissions page, copy the bot token (it starts with xoxb-), and paste both tokens here.
slack.allowed_hint: Slack member ids (like U01ABCDEF), separated by commas. Anyone else gets a pairing code to approve here.
slack.how: Invite the app to a channel with /invite, then mention it or message it directly.

matrix.intro: The agent answers through a Matrix account. Make one for the bot on your homeserver; the hub asks the server about it before saving.
matrix.step1: Create an account for the bot on a Matrix homeserver (in Element, for example).
matrix.step2: Sign in to Element with that account and copy the Access Token from Settings → Help & About.
matrix.step3: Enter the homeserver address (like https://matrix.org) and paste the token here.
matrix.allowed_hint: Full Matrix ids (like @sara:matrix.org), separated by commas. Anyone else gets a pairing code.
matrix.how: Invite the bot's account to a room, or start a direct chat with it. Matrix's library is downloaded on first start.

mattermost.intro: The agent answers through a Mattermost bot account. The hub asks the server about the account before saving.
mattermost.step1: In Mattermost open Integrations → Bot Accounts → Add Bot Account (a system admin turns them on).
mattermost.step2: Pick a name for the bot and copy the token shown after it is made.
mattermost.step3: Enter your server's address (like https://chat.example.com) and paste the token here.
mattermost.allowed_hint: Mattermost user ids, separated by commas. Anyone else gets a pairing code.
mattermost.how: Add the bot to a channel and @mention it, or message it directly.

email.intro: The agent reads a mailbox and answers the mail. The hub signs in to the incoming and outgoing servers before saving; it reads and sends nothing.
email.step1: A mailbox just for the agent is best. In Gmail, turn on 2-Step Verification and make an “app password”.
email.step2: Enter the address, the password and the IMAP and SMTP servers (in Gmail: imap.gmail.com and smtp.gmail.com).
email.step3: Enter the addresses the agent answers. Email sends no pairing code, so anyone not on the list is ignored.
email.allowed_hint: Email addresses, separated by commas. Mail from anyone else is ignored.
email.how: Send a message to the mailbox from an address on the list; the agent answers in the same thread.
